officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirmed `--eval` / `-e` is a documented `bun run` flag ('Evaluate argument as a script. Alias: -e') and that inline eval input is treated as TypeScript-with-JSX, so every acceptance-criterion probe in this PRD (bun -e with an ESM import of a local .ts module) is a supported, non-deprecated invocation. No breaking change or deprecation affecting the probes; nothing else in this issue touches an external library API (the work is pure TypeScript string/regex validation).

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:50]: SEARCH_TOOL_RE is matched against the RAW command text in findStoreReachingSearch (:243-249) before tokenization, so a tool-word match can BEGIN inside a quoted span or inside an unrelated hyphenated token. Combined with recursive:(tool==='rg') (:214) and roots.length===0 => root '.' (:253), any delimited two-letter 'rg' substring anywhere in the command produces a finding. Measured: findStoreReachingSearch('bun run gen-rg-report') -> {root:'.'}; ('grep -q "rg" scripts/cam/patterns.md') -> {root:'.'}; ('test -f docs/x.rg') -> {root:'.'}; ('bash -c "echo rg"') -> {root:'.'}. End-to-end this is a HARD REFUSAL on the issue-filing write path with no bypass: validateSpec returns ok=false for the legitimate criteria '... [oracle: named-command bun run gen-rg-report]' and '... [oracle: named-command grep -q "rg" scripts/cam/patterns.md]', with the misleading diagnostic 'recursive search root "." reaches scripts/cam/issues' for a command that performs no search at all. The second case directly contradicts the module's own documented safe form (:27-30, 'a single-file root under scripts stays legal even with -r') and the tests asserting it (test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts:82-90), flipping only because the search NEEDLE is 'rg'; this is realistic because scripts/cam/patterns.md already contains 'rg ' as a delimited token twice and US-003's own AC3 oracle is exactly the shape grep -q "<needle>" scripts/cam/patterns.md. Fix: require the tool word to be in COMMAND position (start of string, or immediately after a clause separator / '(' / '$(' / 'xargs'), and derive tool candidates from the tokenized stream rather than a raw-text regex scan. Add the missing adversarial cases (tool word inside a quoted needle; tool word as a hyphen-delimited segment of an unrelated token) to test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts and test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts:189]: Two false-negative gaps let a genuinely store-reaching search past the guardrail. (1) applyToken only special-cases token === '--recursive', so the documented long form of -R is missed: findStoreReachingSearch('grep --dereference-recursive zzqqx scripts') -> null, even though man grep defines '-R, --dereference-recursive: Read all files under each directory, recursively'. (2) isStoreReachingRoot (:121-129) normalizes only a leading './' and trailing slashes, so an absolute root reaching the store is missed: findStoreReachingSearch('grep -rl zzqqx /Users/me/repo/scripts') -> null. Both are one-file mechanical fixes (accept '--dereference-recursive' alongside '--recursive'; strip a cwd prefix or match the store suffix for absolute roots) plus their test cases, in the same module the CRITICAL touches.

userStories.notes:
Files: src/issues/spec.ts (validateSpec, :31), test/issues/spec.test.ts (300 lines today, extend it).
- isNonEmptyString ALREADY EXISTS at src/issues/spec.ts:60 (module-private, used by validateSpecSource). Reuse it per element; do not reimplement and do not export it unless a later story needs it across modules.
- Today validateSpec only checks Array.isArray(ac) && ac.length !== 0, so [""] and [123] both pass and are persisted verbatim by buildIssueEntry (src/issues/alloc.ts:161), after which isPlannable's hasAcceptanceCriteria (src/issues/plannable.ts:35) measures only length. Element-level content validation is the single repair site for both symptoms.
- Keep the ValidationResult contract: one human-readable string per error pushed onto errors[], ok === errors.length === 0. Existing callers print each error (validateSpecGuardrail in src/commands/issue-file.ts:219 via printError; issue-specify.ts returns reason 'invalid-spec' with errors).
- validateSpec has TWO callers: the filing guardrail (src/commands/issue-file.ts:219, itself only reached when specSource !== undefined, i.e. --fast-track / --derived-from) and the spec interview (src/commands/issue-specify.ts:332). One rule here covers both ends; plain `cam issue --file-local` filing (stage:idea, no spec) deliberately never reaches the guardrail, so do not widen that gate.
- Do NOT export or re-export validateSpecGuardrail (issue-file.ts:219): it adds no rule of its own and the only runtime export of issue-file.ts is createLocalIssueOnMain.
- Regression risk to check before committing: existing fixtures in test/issue-file.test.ts and test/integration/issue-file-spec-channel.test.ts (e.g. acceptanceCriteria: ['The child issue behaves correctly']) must keep passing; only blank/non-string elements may start failing.
- Per patterns.md Oracle-falsifiability rule (scripts/cam/patterns.md:928), re-sweep the criterion probe RED on unmodified main before trusting it; it was verified exit 1 on main at plan time (2026-07-30).
- Probe-authoring trap (lived while writing the issue): a literal ']' inside a probe string closes the [oracle: ...] mark early (extractLastOracleRaw walks bracket depth), which yields a truncated command and a bash exit 2 that READS like a red sweep. The probes build brackets via String.fromCharCode(91/93) for this reason. If you edit any oracle text, re-drive parseOracleDirective (src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts:227) and diff the extracted command against the intended one; treat exit 2 or a stderr 'syntax error' as an extraction failure, never as red.

userStories.notes:
Depends on US-001 (same function, same test file). Files: ONE new leaf detector module (recommended src/issues/self-contaminating-search.ts), src/issues/spec.ts, plus tests (new test/issues/self-contaminating-search.test.ts and/or extend test/issues/spec.test.ts).
- SHARED DETECTOR IS LOAD-BEARING: US-003 wires the plan-time lint rule to this SAME exported predicate. Two parallel implementations would drift and let filing accept what plan time blocks (or the reverse), so export one predicate (e.g. findStoreReachingSearch(command): { root: string } | null) from a leaf module both sides import. src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts has zero imports of its own, so importing parseOracleDirective from src/issues/* creates no cycle; verify with `bun run typecheck`.
- Extract the criterion's oracle command with the project's own parser (parseOracleDirective, src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts:227), never a hand-rolled regex; scan only named-command / file-assert directives, exactly like lintStoryCriteria (src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:656).
- Recommended detection core, purely lexical and I/O-free (validateSpec must stay pure): a search invocation is recursive when it is grep/egrep/fgrep carrying -r/-R (bundled or separate) or rg (recursive by default); a root is STORE-REACHING when it is '.' , or a directory-ancestor-or-self of scripts/cam/issues ('scripts', 'scripts/cam', 'scripts/cam/issues', with or without a trailing slash), or when the invocation carries NO positional path at all (search defaults to cwd). The ancestor test makes the file-vs-directory distinction fall out for free: 'scripts/cam/patterns.md' is not an ancestor of the store, so a single-file root under scripts stays legal even with -r, and 'docs/adr/' is legal.
- Do NOT refuse a criterion merely for having no oracle, and do not require an oracle: many legitimate filings carry prose-only criteria, and requiring oracles here is a different (out-of-scope) gate. Only the contaminated FORM is refused.
- Blessed idiom that must stay ACCEPTED: pinpoint store read, `file-assert git show main:scripts/cam/issues/CAM-XXXX.json`, prescribed by .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md:102. It names a path, it does not descend.
- Explicit store exclusion must stay ACCEPTED: `--exclude-dir=issues` (and equivalent pathspec/glob exclusions) is exactly the shape of the intended repair for CAM-460 AC2, so refusing it would break the very fix this rule is meant to enable.
- Terminology: the new class is 'self-contaminating oracle'. patterns.md already uses 'self-nullifying' 5 times for a DIFFERENT defect (a zero-match scan passing in silence). Do not conflate the two terms.
- Sweep the criterion probe RED on unmodified main first (verified exit 1 at plan time, 2026-07-30) and re-drive parseOracleDirective on the probe text after any edit; a literal ']' truncates the mark and the resulting bash exit 2 reads as a false red (see US-001 notes).

Swept RED on main 2026-07-30: exit 1, ambas as ancoras com count 0; controle positivo com ancora existente (Oracle-falsifiability rule) sai 0. A espinha de qualidade passa. Este criterio e gate de nao-regressao, nao detector de mudanca: e verde na main hoje por construcao e nao foi varrido vermelho. [oracle: named-command bun run check:all]

- patterns.md bullet: name the term 'self-contaminating oracle', state the distinction between a pinpoint store read and a store-reaching recursive root, and cite the explicit-exclusion (--exclude-dir) safe form; both anchors are asserted by the probe. Follow the file's existing bullet style (bold lead-in, US/CAM/date attribution) and append, never truncate.
- Prose line references to patterns.md:899 are stale (the falsifiability rule lives at :928); do NOT renumber line references in this story, it is out of scope.
- Re-sweep all four issue-derived probes RED on unmodified main before trusting them (each verified exit 1 at plan time, 2026-07-30, except the check:all criterion, which is a non-regression gate that is green on main by construction).
